WHY 2.0? // FULL BODY, NOT JUST THE CONTROLLER

THE WRIST COULD FAKE IT.
THE BODY CAN'T.

Earlier controller-based Just Dance scoring followed the hand holding the motion controller—not the whole dancer. You could sit down, move your wrist, and still register the move.

Just Dance 2.0 extracts the dancer's body pose and scores the movement itself.

THENONE HAND → 2.0BODY POSE
CONTROLLER ≠ BODYFULL-POSE REVIEW
03

HOW IT WORKS // LOCAL, VIDEO IN

TWO VIDEOS IN.
CLEAR FEEDBACK OUT.

MediaPipe extracts body pose from the reference and performance. Dynamic Time Warping aligns the sequences, then geometry-based scoring compares angles, limb direction, distance, and posture.

  1. 01INPUT

    Choose a reference video and your performance.

  2. 02EXTRACT

    MediaPipe extracts the centered dancer's body pose frame by frame.

  3. 03ALIGN

    Dynamic Time Warping matches the two pose sequences in time.

  4. 04SCORE

    See overall, timing, arms, legs, and torso scores.

FRAME BY FRAMEDTW ALIGNED
04

WHAT THE SCORE MEANS // GEOMETRY

NOT A BLACK BOX.
JUST THE MOVEMENT.

The scorer is local, deterministic, and geometry-only. It weights joint angles, limb directions, scale-free distances, and posture; unreliable joints are ignored.

OFFLINE DESKTOP APP — pose extraction and comparison run locally.

BEYOND K-POP // SAME PIPELINE, NEW MOVEMENT

DANCE FIRST.
ANY WORKOUT NEXT.

The comparison engine is not tied to K-pop. Give it a repeatable reference and it can help review other workouts, drills, and movement practice.
